subject: Culture
title: When Gifts Are Bribes
description: A quick win: understand When Gifts Are Bribes.

hook.text: In South Korea, giving a government official a gift over $45 is a criminal offense since the Kim Young-ran Act.

buildup.text: The line between gift and bribe shifts across cultures. What's hospitality in one country is corruption in another.

discovery.text: The US Foreign Corrupt Practices Act criminalizes gifts to foreign officials. Many Asian business customs violate it.

twist.text: In parts of Africa and South Asia, refusing a gift from a business partner is the real offense—it signals distrust.

climax.text: Multinational companies now train employees on gift thresholds for every country. Cultural fluency prevents jail.

punchline.text: One culture's courtesy is another's felony.

quiz.question: What is the gift limit for South Korean officials under the Kim Young-ran Act?

details.summary: The line between a gift and a bribe shifts dramatically across cultures. A bottle of wine for a doctor is normal in France but potentially corrupt in the US. Corporate gift limits vary by country. What one culture calls relationship-building, another calls criminal corruption.
details.whyItMatters: The gift-bribe boundary has enormous legal and ethical consequences. Multinational companies operate across conflicting gift norms where cultural generosity can become criminal liability.
takeaways: US Foreign Corrupt Practices Act criminalizes gifts to foreign officials
Many Asian business cultures require gift-giving to build trust
The distinction between gift and bribe is culturally determined

faq.question: When does a gift become a bribe?
faq.answer: Legally, it depends on jurisdiction, intent, value, and the recipient's official capacity. A gift given with no expectation of return is generally legal; one given to influence an official decision is a bribe.

faq.question: How do multinational companies navigate gift culture?
faq.answer: Companies operating internationally must balance local gift customs with anti-corruption laws like the US FCPA and UK Bribery Act. Most set internal gift value limits ($25-$100), require disclosure, and train employees on local customs.
